blossom.name: Blossom Court
blossom.blurb: A walled sakura garden around a lotus fountain. Mirrored starts, so neither side has the shorter road.

canyon.name: Sunscar Canyon
canyon.blurb: A red-rock chasm with two rope bridges. The oasis road runs along both rims, close enough to shout across but not to touch.

citadel.name: Sunken Citadel
citadel.blurb: A drowned fortress at low tide. Its halls and causeways mirror each other for both teams.

cross.name: Crossroads Ruins
cross.blurb: Four old roads meet at a sun plaza. Each fighter starts in a corner. Seat 2, 3 or 4 players; with 2, use opposite corners.

fjord.name: Frozen Fjord
fjord.blurb: A frozen fjord between two clans. Only the north and south bridges cross it, so the ice shelves become a long standoff.

frost.name: Frostfang Pass
frost.blurb: A mountain pass wrapped around a frozen lake. Two ridge trails meet over the ice; everything else is a slog through snow.

glade.name: Hollow Oak Glade
glade.blurb: A ring of trails around an ancient hollow oak. Ferns choke the gaps, so the long way round is often the only way round.

harbor.name: Saltmarsh Harbor
harbor.blurb: A tidal river splits the market from the wharf. Only two bridges cross it, so whoever holds them controls the fight.

ironwood.name: Ironwood Crossing
ironwood.blurb: Two warbands meet at the ford of an old forest. Point-symmetric: both sides walk the same roads.

isle.name: Four Winds Isle
isle.blurb: An island ringed by surf with a salt lake at its heart. Four beacons mark the shortcuts between the coves.

keeps.name: Twin Keeps
keeps.blurb: Two keeps face each other across a river with three bridges. Six fighters, two banners, one road through the middle.

moot.name: Woodland Moot
moot.blurb: Four groves around an old standing-stone circle. Short board, fast fights: every corner is two moves from the stones.

moss.name: Mossgate Abbey
moss.blurb: A drowned abbey swallowed by the fen. Broken walls funnel both teams toward the altar at its heart.

star.name: Pentacle Ruins
star.blurb: Five arms around a moonstone circle. Built for up to five heroes; every tip is a start.

valley.name: Greatwood Valley
valley.blurb: A stream splits an old-growth valley. Two footbridges and a line of stepping stones are the only dry crossings.
